ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is the input voltage U1, with the upper end positive and the lower end negative; the positive input terminal first passes through the series resistor R to reach the upper output node on the right side. Between this output node and the common negative terminal below, two branches are connected in parallel: the middle branch is the voltage-regulator diode VZ, and the right branch is the load resistor RL. The output voltage Uo is marked across the two ends of RL, with the upper end positive and the lower end negative. Therefore, this is a parallel-type voltage-regulator circuit with a series resistor plus a parallel voltage-regulator diode and load. Reasoning: It is known that the voltage-regulating value of VZ is 6 V, R = 500 Ω, RL = 1 kΩ, and the input U1 varies between 3 V and 12 V. When the voltage-regulator diode has not broken down, the output is obtained by voltage division of R and RL: Uo = U1 × RL / (R + RL) = U1 × 1000 / (500 + 1000) = 2U1/3. When this divided voltage value reaches 6 V, the voltage-regulator diode begins voltage regulation: 2U1/3 = 6, so U1 = 9 V. Therefore, when U1 increases from 3 V to 9 V, Uo increases from 2 V to 6 V. When U1 goes from 9 V to 12 V, the voltage-regulator diode clamps the output at 6 V. Checking when U1 = 12 V, the series resistor current is (12 - 6)/500 = 12 mA, the load current is 6/1000 = 6 mA, and the remaining current can flow through the voltage-regulator diode, so voltage regulation is established. Therefore, the load voltage range is 2 V to 6 V.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify a shunt zener regulator: R is in series with the source, while VZ and RL are parallel at the output. From the text take VZ=6 V, R=500 Ω, RL=1 kΩ, and U1 ranges from 3 V to 12 V. With the zener off, Uo=U1*RL/(R+RL)=U1*1000/(500+1000)=2U1/3. Breakdown starts when this divider value reaches 6 V, so U1=9 V. Thus for U1 from 3 V to 9 V, Uo goes from 2 V to 6 V. For U1 from 9 V to 12 V, the zener clamps Uo at 6 V; verify at 12 V that series current (12-6)/500=12 mA exceeds load current 6/1000=6 mA, so regulation is feasible. Therefore the load voltage range is 2 to 6 V.

method.method_draft: Describe the image first as a source U1 feeding R, then an output node with RL and VZ both to the lower rail. Let Uo be the node voltage. Apply KCL: (U1-Uo)/R = Uo/RL + Iz.
